archetype: Mono-black aristocrats-combo, and for the first time every artifact agrees. deck-audit reads the archetype 'combo' off strategic_frame.json and applies its overrides (tutors 4-8, protection 4-6). goldfish_targets.json was re-derived against the thirteen checker-passed stacks, so the declared engine and the verified engine are now the same object: four independent kills — two of them unbounded (009 self-funding, 011 free), two lethal but bounded (010 by the library, 012 by its own termination) — sharing a three-card drain slot and one recursive body. Three of the four name neither the commander nor Nest of Scarabs, which is why the archetype's best-known failure mode — removal on Yawgmoth — does not describe this list.
verdict: It functions, its enablers turn over, and it converts: four checker-passed kills that each take a four-opponent pod from 40 to 0 — two unbounded (009 self-funding, 011 paying nothing at all), 012 lethal precisely because it terminates, and only 010 spending a resource from outside the loop, at 39 of the 59 draws its library permits. Feed the Swarm bought the enchantment class and moved interaction-breadth from 1 to 2 of 5, and that is still what binds — but the finding is now much narrower than it was. A regex over all 79 maindeck oracle texts returns exactly one match for destroying or exiling an artifact, a land or a nonland permanent, and it is Fatal Push's mana-value clause: the artifact class and the land class are at literal zero, and artifacts are where this deck's hosers live. Everything else is at or above target, and the honest answer to 'what else should change' is very little.

gaps: THERE IS NO UNION RATE AND NOTHING SHOULD QUOTE ONE. goldfish_targets.json's own _no_union_target key says why: goldfish._target_met evaluates each need group independently, so a hand of Exquisite Blood, Gravecrawler and Zulaport Cutthroat satisfies three groups while assembling no kill. Four independent kills therefore have no single assembled_rate, and the four per-kill figures (0.011 / 0.005 / 0.069 / 0.046) are the only honest ones.

interaction-breadth IS A FLOOR AND WILL STAY ONE. The heuristic only inspects cards that already carry an interactive role, so Bojuka Bog (land:tapped) answers a graveyard invisibly and Strip Mine (land:utility) would answer a land invisibly. The number will read 2 or 3 for a deck that covers four classes. Read the cards; I did, and the artifact class is genuinely zero.

card-advantage IS UNDERSTATED BY SIX, NOT FIVE. The audit's probe names Ayara, Black Market Connections, Castle Locthwain, Plumb the Forbidden and Yawgmoth. card_roles.json files Necropotence as 'stax' alone and its oracle text never uses the word 'draw', so the probe misses it too. The best card-advantage engine in mono-black contributes nothing to the count.

NONE OF THE FOUR ADDS IS OWNED. owned_candidates.json lists 148 cards the pilot already holds and Gate to Phyrexia, Strip Mine and Bloodthirsty Conqueror are not among them; Ophiomancer is (in 'Golgari Parts'). Prices are stripped from cards.csv, so nothing here weighs acquisition cost, and Strip Mine in particular is a real purchase for a land slot.

EVERY LINE THIS PAGE OPENS IS UNVERIFIED. Bloodthirsty Conqueror's pairings carry 'needs a stack scenario' by design, and so does the Plunderer/Ashnod's/Skeleton mana line. 32 combo lines are contained in this deck and 11 are tagged two-card infinites; containment is a shortlist, and the checker has already refuted a Commander Spellbook tag on this deck once.

THE -1/-1 SUBTHEME IS UNADJUDICATED. Nest of Scarabs, Soul Snuffers, Skinrender, Black Sun's Zenith, Massacre Girl, Sinister Gnarlbark, Persist, Fume Spitter and Ifnir Deadlands serve an engine that stacks 002 and 005 cap at 5 to 8 activations — a value ceiling, not a kill — while three of the four verified kills never touch it. deck_recon's own gaps say no dated source compares that subtheme to pure aristocrats. I am not proposing to unpick it: Nest of Scarabs is on the board in nine checker-passed scenarios, six of them presentable (its name appears in twelve, nine of them presentable — 009, 010 and 012 name it only as absent from the board), and cutting it would cost more than it could plausibly buy. But that is the largest unexamined block in the list and it is why my cut list is three cards long rather than eight.

RECON IS DATED. deck_recon.json carries as_of 2026-08-03 and no artifact in this repo holds per-commander inclusion rates. The Ophiomancer case leans on it and is ranked last for exactly that reason: an inclusion rate is a fact about other people's decks.

findings.note: NEW, found on the independent sweep. 'Two of the four name neither the commander nor Nest of Scarabs' is THREE of four, and the same artifact says so two blocks later. goldfish_targets.json carries commander: true on KILL D alone; KILLS A, B and C name no commander in any need group. Nest of Scarabs appears in NO kill's need groups at all, and stack 012's assumptions state 'Nest of Scarabs is NOT on the battlefield' verbatim, so the by-board reading gives the same three (009, 011, 012 carry neither; 010 carries Yawgmoth). lean_into[0] says 'a commander who is not on three of them' with evidence.commander_gated 'only KILL D (stack 010)', which is the correct count — so the artifact contradicts itself. The error runs AGAINST the diagnosis's own thesis (it understates the deck's independence from its commander, which is the archetype line's whole point). Note for the orchestrator: strategic_frame.json's overall_assessment carries the identical sentence ('Two of the four need neither the commander nor Nest of Scarabs'), so this is inherited and both should move together. Also loose in the same sentence: 'sharing a three-card drain slot and one recursive body' — the three-card drain any_of is shared by A, B and D only (C's drain group is South Wind Avatar / Marauding Blight-Priest / Starscape Cleric) and Gravecrawler is in A and B only.

The two-of-four recount landed and its conclusion is right, but the clause justifying it is false against goldfish_targets.json. 'KILL A's and KILL D's drain groups are all creatures' — that group is {Bastion of Remembrance, Zulaport Cutthroat, Ayara, First of Locthwain} minus one, i.e. three cards, and Bastion of Remembrance's type_line in cards.json is 'Enchantment'. Two of the three are creatures. The correct statement is the one the number rests on: A and D can be SATISFIED entirely out of creatures (Zulaport or Ayara), which is why neither strictly requires a noncreature permanent. As written the clause also contradicts the first half of the same sentence, which correctly places Bastion — an enchantment — on 009's and 010's boards; I read all four kill boards again card by card and they are exactly as the axis lists them (Bastion in 009/010/011, Phyrexian Altar in 011, Exquisite Blood in 012). Verdict 'weakness' and the shape argument are sound: Lightning Greaves grants shroud to the equipped creature, Sedgemoor Witch's ward and Yahenni's indestructible are self-only, so none of the three can save an enchantment or an artifact.
